questions.explanation:
GitHub Actions supports the `issues` event with the `opened` and `edited` activity types, and the `issue_comment` event with the `created` activity type. The `issue_comment` event applies to comments on both issues and pull requests. Consequently, the workflow runs when an issue is created (opened) or edited, or when a comment is created on an issue or pull request.

**Learn more:** [GitHub Actions events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)

options.text: .github/workflow-templates

questions.explanation:
GitHub Actions workflow templates intended for the New workflow interface are placed in the `workflow-templates` directory of an organization’s `.github` repository. Standard executable workflow files instead use `.github/workflows`; template display also relies on an associated metadata file in the template directory.\

questions.question: As a developer, you are using a Docker container action in your workflow. What must be in place for the action to run successfully?

options.text: The job env must be set to a Linux environment.
The action must be published to the GitHub Marketplace.
The referenced action must be hosted on Docker Hub.
The job runs-on must specify a Linux machine with Docker installed.

questions.explanation:
Docker container actions must run on a Linux runner. For self-hosted runners, Docker must be installed; therefore, the job’s `runs-on` configuration must target a Linux machine with Docker available. GitHub’s workflow syntax documentation states that Docker container actions require a Linux runner and that self-hosted Linux runners require Docker to be installed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)

questions.question: When creating and managing custom actions in an enterprise environment, which of the following is a best practice?

options.text: creating a separate repository for each action so that the version can be managed independently
creating a separate branch in application repositories that only contains the actions
creating a single repository for all custom actions so that the versions for each action are all the same
including custom actions that other teams need to reference in the same repository as application code

questions.explanation:
Custom actions intended for use by other teams should be kept in their own repositories. This decouples each action’s versioning, tracking, and release lifecycle from application code, allowing it to be managed independently.\
\
**Learn more:** [Managing custom actions — GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud%40latest/actions/how-tos/create-and-publish-actions/manage-custom-actions)

Add the deployment webhook event as a trigger for the workflow when the code quality integration is completed

questions.explanation:
A third-party Checks API integration creates and updates a check run. GitHub Actions can trigger a workflow from the `check_run` event, including when the check run is `completed`, which provides the appropriate completion signal for the code-quality integration.

**Learn more:** [Events that trigger workflows — GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)

questions.explanation:

You must perform a task that requires executing a custom script in a GitHub Actions workflow. The script must execute within the workflow environment and must not require an external container or prebuilt image.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a run step
a JavaScript action
a composite action
a Docker container action

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Which command below sets the `$FOO` environment variable within a script so that subsequent workflow job steps can use it?

options.text: run: echo \
run: echo \

questions.explanation:
Appending `FOO=bar` to the `GITHUB_ENV` environment file makes `FOO` available to all subsequent steps in the same GitHub Actions job. The shell process that writes the entry does not itself receive the new value.\
\
**Learn more:** [Workflow commands for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands?apiVersion=2022-11-28&tool=bash)

questions.question: An organization’s policies allow only local actions. How should actions be distributed for this organization?

options.text: via a repository owned by a third party
via repositories owned by the organization
via the GitHub Marketplace
via the .github repository owned by the organization

questions.explanation:
A local-actions-only GitHub Actions policy permits actions and reusable workflows that exist within the organization. Hosting actions in repositories owned by that organization satisfies the policy; third-party repositories and GitHub Marketplace actions do not.\
\
**Learn more:** [Disabling or limiting GitHub Actions for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization)

Leverage the actions/download-secret action in the workflow.
Store the dataset in a GitHub encrypted secret.
Create a GitHub encrypted secret with the Large object option selected and upload the dataset.
Compress the dataset.

questions.explanation:
GitHub Actions secrets have a 48-KB size limit. For a 10-MB protected file, the supported approach is to encrypt the dataset and store only its decryption passphrase or key in a GitHub encrypted secret; the encrypted file must be stored separately, such as committed to the repository, then decrypted during the workflow. The required encrypted-file storage step is not among the choices, so there are only two technically correct listed steps.

**Learn more:** [Using secrets in GitHub Actions — Storing large secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets?tool=webui) · [GitHub Actions secrets reference](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud%40latest/actions/reference/security/secrets)

questions.question: How can you print a debug message in your workflow?

options.text: echo \
echo \
echo \
echo \

questions.explanation:
GitHub Actions emits a debug log message through the `debug` workflow command, using the `::debug::message` syntax. Debug messages are shown when step debug logging is enabled.\
\
**Learn more:** [Workflow commands for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands)

questions.question: As a developer, how do you identify a composite action on GitHub?

options.text: The action’s repository name includes the keyword “composite.”
The action’s repository includes an init.sh file in the root directory.
The action’s repository includes Dockerfile and package.json files.
The action.yml metadata file has the runs.using value set to composite.

questions.explanation:
A GitHub composite action is declared in its `action.yml` metadata by setting the required `runs.using` field to `composite`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Metadata syntax reference — GitHub Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/metadata-syntax?learn=create_actions)

questions.question: In which of the following situations should self-hosted runners be used? (Each correct answer provides a complete solution. Choose two.)

options.text: when the workflow jobs must be run on Windows 10
when jobs must run for longer than 6 hours
when a workflow job needs to install software from the local network
when GitHub Actions minutes must be used for the workflow runs
when you want to use macOS runners

questions.explanation:
GitHub-hosted runners limit each job to six hours of execution time, whereas self-hosted runners can support longer-running jobs. Self-hosted runners also provide control over the execution environment, including access to software available on a local network.\
\
**Learn more:** [Self-hosted runners](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/self-hosted-runners) · [Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)

questions.question: While awaiting approval, after how many days in the “Waiting” state does a workflow automatically fail?

options.text: 30 days
60 days
14 days
7 days

questions.explanation:
Power Automate counts pending approval steps toward a cloud flow’s maximum 30-day run duration. When that limit is reached, pending steps time out and the flow fails.\
\
